explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares LLM-as-a-judge ratings with human expert ratings, stating they were 'strongly correlated' and reporting a Pearson correlation coefficient.

prompts.notes: Paper mentions prompts were based on six evaluation criteria, with detailed prompts and scoring method in Appendix B and C, but full prompts are not shown in provided text.

guidelines.notes: Detailed evaluation criteria provided in Appendix Section A; experts rated on 5-point scale for six clinical criteria; each summary independently rated by 2 experts in blind study.

shared_criteria: inclusion of important positive clinical details
inclusion of important negative clinical details

sample_size.notes: Exact number of summaries used for validation not explicitly stated; validation performed on summaries generated from human transcripts (LLM-Eval-H scenario).

quantitative_scores.notes: Correlation reported between LLM-as-Judge ratings (LLM-Eval-H) and human expert ratings; applies to composite evaluation across all six criteria.

validation_results.summary_finding: LLM-as-Judge ratings showed strong correlation (Pearson=0.816) with human expert ratings, consistent with prior work demonstrating LLMs can effectively replicate human judgments for medical conversation summarization evaluation.

shared_criteria: inclusion of important positive clinical details
inclusion of important negative clinical details
criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM-as-Judge and human experts evaluated summaries using the same six clinical criteria on identical 5-point scales; no criteria were evaluated by only one method.
